text:
oncall-bot: Paging: Sev 2 — multiple PrivateLink customers in eu-central-azc reporting PrivateLink endpoints resolving to public ELB IPs and traffic egressing out of azd. Triggered by DNS+routing anomalies. Incident channel open.

alejandra: grabbing context — seeing a spike in DNS answers from our azc-dns cluster returning public ELB addresses for svc-privlink-prod.api.redwood.internal. Customers report inability to reach private endpoints, requests time out or go to external LB.

mike: I can confirm. Dig from a customer peering vpc shows:
```
; <<>> DiG 9.11.3 <<>> svc-privlink-prod.api.redwood.internal @10.10.20.5
;; ANSWER SECTION:
svc-privlink-prod.api.redwood.internal. 30 IN A 18.204.12.34
```
That 18.204.12.34 is an external ELB IP in another AZ — not expected.

luca: checking BGP/route state in eu-central-azc. I'm seeing a recent route-map change pushed to the edge-azc-router at 2026-03-15T17:14Z that rewrites next-hop for 10.0.0.0/16 to advertise via transit-aws-east. Suspect someone pushed a proxy egress override.

alejandra: who pushed that change? deploy-bot: any recent infra rollouts?

deploy-bot: Automated change: edge-router-config v2.19.4 deployed at 2026-03-15T17:13:58 by infra-ci. Change-id: infra/edge/2026-03-15/arn:config/7261.

mike: that aligns with customer reports — timeline matches. Also seeing DNS server logs with rewrite rule applied that maps internal hostname to external ELB for certain AZs. Could be a bad template in the config that toggles dns-rewrite=true for privatelink zones.

luca: snapshot of router config diff (relevant lines):
```
- route-map PRIV_ROUTES permit 10
-  set ip next-hop local
+ route-map PRIV_ROUTES permit 10
+  set ip next-hop 18.204.0.1
```
That 18.204.0.1 is our egress NAT appliance in a different AZ that translates and sends traffic to public ELB.

alejandra: ok, scope of impact — preliminary list of customers with PrivateLink endpoints in azc: AcmeCorp, BetaAnalytics, Fintegral. CS has opened tickets. sara_cs, can you confirm customer-facing impact?

sara_cs: AcmeCorp reporting 503s starting ~17:16Z, BetaAnalytics seeing ~40% of requests failing, Fintegral is degraded (failover to backup endpoint triggered). All three on Dedicated PrivateLink peering. I've notified account teams and asked them to escalate to customer SREs.

tom: I'll take the on-call handoff in 15 mins (taking over at 17:45Z). Alejandra, if you can prepare rollback steps I'll run them.

alejandra: rollback plan: 1) revert edge-router-config to v2.19.3 on azc (removes the next-hop rewrite) 2) revert dns-rewrite flag in azc-dns config 3) monitor DNS answers and BGP updates, verify private A records point to internal NLB IPs. Steps below.

alejandra: rollback commands (edge-router):
```
# rollback to prior config
sudo /opt/infra/bin/apply-config --device edge-azc-router --config v2.19.3
# verify BGP
show bgp neighbors summary | grep Established
show ip route 10.0.0.0/16
```

alejandra: dns rollback (azc-dns cluster):
```
kubectl -n infra set image deployment/azc-dns azc-dns=azc-dns:2026.03.10
kubectl rollout status deployment/azc-dns
# verify
dig @10.10.20.5 svc-privlink-prod.api.redwood.internal
```

mike: while rollback runs, we should add temporary mitigations for affected customers: 1) add static host overrides in our egress DNS to point these hostnames to internal NLB IPs 2) announce more specific /32 route for the NLB IPs in azc to prefer local path.

luca: possible faster fix: remove the erroneous route-map from edge-azc-router instead of full config rollback. I'll prepare a single-line removal:
```
conf t
no route-map PRIV_ROUTES permit 10
end
write
```

alejandra: good idea. Tom — want to run that when you take over?

tom: yep. I'll run the no route-map command at 17:46Z and coordinate with mike to watch DNS. Tom -> running now.

oncall-bot: command executed by tom at 2026-03-15T17:46:02Z: no route-map PRIV_ROUTES permit 10

luca: bgp flaps seen for ~30s, now neighbors re-established. Checking route table — NLB internal IPs show local next-hop again.

mike: re-running dig from a customer VPC:
```
; <<>> DiG 9.11.3 <<>> svc-privlink-prod.api.redwood.internal @10.10.20.5
;; ANSWER SECTION:
svc-privlink-prod.api.redwood.internal. 30 IN A 10.200.5.12
```
10.200.5.12 is internal NLB IP in azc — good.

sara_cs: customer updates: AcmeCorp confirms connectivity restored at 17:48Z. BetaAnalytics reports errors dropped to <1%. Fintegral is still seeing sporadic retries but failing rate down from 40% to 5%.

alejandra: rolling back dns-rewrite flag now to be safe. Performing kubectl image rollback.

deploy-bot: Deployment azc-dns rolled to azc-dns:2026.03.10 by infra-ci at 2026-03-15T17:52:11Z.

mike: monitoring telemetry: tokenized traces show successful private path for >99% of requests after 17:50Z. We'll keep elevated monitoring for 2 hours.

tom: handing back to alejandro (original owner) at 18:15Z. Leaving a few followups: 1) postmortem draft, 2) add unit test to infra config pipeline to prevent dns-rewrite flag in privatelink zones, 3) add canary gating for route-map changes.

alejandra: noted. I'll own the postmortem. Preliminary RCA: infra config template regression in edge-router config allowed next-hop rewrite and dns-rewrite flag to be enabled in azc for privatelink zone. Change made by infra-ci without canary.

sara_cs: I'm opening customer communications with timeline and mitigation notes. Will attach logs for AcmeCorp and BetaAnalytics.

mike: next actions for SRE/infra: - revert template in config repo - add CI test to disallow dns-rewrite for zone=privatelink - schedule a follow-up with infra team for canary rollout policy.

luca: I'll also add BGP dampening config to reduce churn risk and add monitoring alert for next-hop rewrite diffs.

oncall-bot: Incident state -> mitigated at 2026-03-15T18:00:00Z. Postmortem owner: alejandra. Severity downgraded to sev 3 for follow-ups.

alejandra: thanks everyone. Closing the incident channel once postmortem skeleton is up. :white_check_mark:
